items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...James Paul was. I wonder if they had any bands at boxing matches in it. Have you come across that? [INTERVIEWEE] I don't know. I haven't come across any such thing...

ctx.x: He had to have papers that would show that, or at least it would be advisable for him to have his papers of freedom on them all the time. However, New Orleans was not like a lot of the rest of the South, at least up until the 1850s, and I mean, did it even begin to crack down. It was a much more tolerant, lenient city. The Negroes of the city had a society of some sort that they called the Philharmonic Society prior to the Civil War, and I've even seen the tantalizing indications that possibly white musicians…
Caldwell also was involved in promoting boxing, you know, the early theater, James Paul was. I wonder if they had any bands at boxing matches in it. Have you come across that?

I don't know. I haven't come across any such thing, and I've perused all the papers as closely as I can, but I'm not so sure, and I'm getting outside of anything I know much about, but I'm not so sure it was boxing. Very well known then, they might have had a boxer that they brought over or something like this, but Well they had them. I tend to think of boxing as post-Civil War.
